working_title: Kent's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Sandwich, Deal, Littlestone and Beyond
angle: Kent has three Open Championship-pedigree links packed into a tiny stretch of coastline, yet most visiting golfers only tick off Royal St George's and leave. This post maps the full Sandwich-to-Romney circuit, tells readers which clubs actually let visitors on and when, and flags the under-the-radar alternatives worth adding to the trip.
research_notes:
- Kent has more than 80 affiliated golf clubs and roughly 100 courses countywide, with three Open Championship venues clustered on its east coast near Sandwich and Deal (Royal St George's, Royal Cinque Ports, Prince's).
- Royal St George's, Sandwich: current Open rota venue; par 70, 7,204 yards; visitor access is restricted and tee times fill quickly — booking well in advance or playing as a member's guest is strongly advised.
- Royal Cinque Ports (Deal): one of England's toughest links; welcomes visitors on weekdays; removed from the Open rota but served as a Final Qualifying Course most recently in 2025.
- Prince's Golf Club, Sandwich: sits immediately next to Royal St George's; offers 27 holes across three 9-hole loops (Dunes, Shore, Himalayas); 17 of the 27 original greens were salvaged after World War Two; accommodation available at The Lodge at Prince's and a restaurant (Brasserie on the Bay) on site.
- Littlestone Golf Club, New Romney: founded 1888; par 71, 6,486 yards; championship links laid out on naturally undulating land between Romney Marsh and the English Channel; original layout by Laidlaw Purves, with input from James Braid, Alister MacKenzie, Frank Pennink, Donald Steel and Peter Alliss over its history; bunkering revamped in 2021/22; ranked Britain & Ireland's 136th best course (Golf World, 2026); visitors welcome weekdays and weekends (after 11:30 on Sundays); high-season visitor fee on the Championship Links: £160 for 18 holes (source: where2golf, updated 2026 — flag for verification before publish).
- Walmer & Kingsdown Golf Club: clifftop course near Deal, designed by James Braid; described as a unique location course with the White Cliffs backdrop; a quieter, more affordable option.
- North Foreland Golf Club, Broadstairs: clifftop layout at the northern end of the county offering sea views; a parkland-meets-links blend.
- Westgate & Birchington Golf Club: short, affordable seaside course near Margate; par 64, 4,896 yards; a good warm-up or budget option.
- The stretch around Sandwich and Deal is widely described as one of the driest microclimates in England — worth noting for year-round playability.
- Practical logistics: Canterbury or Sandwich are suggested bases for the east Kent links circuit; midweek play generally gives better rates and quieter courses.
- Do NOT fabricate specific prices for Royal St George's, Royal Cinque Ports, or Prince's beyond what appears above; describe them in general terms (premium championship green fees) rather than inventing figures.
